dedupe_keys.name: multi energy district heating network control study rule based versus model predictive control in modelica on the pegase platform

description: This record describes a 2025 arXiv study of operational control strategies for a multi-energy district heating network. Two strategies are compared: a reactive rule-based control and a model predictive control (MPC). A small district heating network is modelled in Modelica, with a production plant combining a heat pump, a gas boiler and a thermal solar field, a storage tank for flexibility, and virtual buildings aggregated into a single consumer. The authors implement both strategies on their co-simulation and control platform, called Pegase. Both aim to meet demand within technical constraints, and MPC also minimises operating cost given variable electricity prices and solar thermal availability. Scenarios vary the heat plant sizing and the forecasting error. The abstract reports that operating cost falls when switching from rule-based control to MPC, especially with variable energy costs, intermittent solar energy and storage. Coverage is a small virtual district heating network. Access: the paper on arXiv, free; no code or licence is stated on the pages read. Caveats: a small virtual network, not a measured system. It suits control design for heat networks, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
